method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across service as pilgrimage and the interrupted journey, mutual longing, wisdom and the life of the community, care for health, livelihood and travel, patient postponement, service needed at home, companions and relatives, timing and routes, individual welcomes, pilgrimage on another’s behalf, and arrival, gratitude and return. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Thou art permitted to come, but next year.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits the believer to come, but next year; a terse example of a deferred permission.

selected.text: We have made several pilgrimages on your behalf
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a believer that He has made several pilgrimages on their behalf.

selected.text: You and friends have permission to come to New York.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s cablegram of November 1912 permits a believer and friends to come to New York; permission for a visit during His travels.

selected.text: Rest assured that I shall soon see your delicate little face
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assures a child He will soon see their delicate little face; tenderness in welcome.

selected.text: Thou art permitted to come alone to visit this luminous Spot.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer to come alone to the luminous Spot.

selected.text: If you have great longing to attain my presence, you are permitted.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: You have permission to visit the Holy Shrine without family members.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a visit to the Holy Shrine without family members.

selected.text: O my dear son! If you wish to travel to America, you have permission.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tenderly permits His “dear son” to travel to America.

selected.text: His honor, Mirza Ahmad Sohrab, has been permitted to leave for America
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá records that Mirza Ahmad Sohrab has been permitted to leave for America.

selected.text: Whenever thou desirest, thou art permitted to proceed from here to India
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer to proceed from the Holy Land to India whenever they wish.

selected.text: Haji Rida has attained the presence. He must give thanks to God for this.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says Haji Rida has attained the presence and must give thanks to God for it.

selected.text: Write that they should come on Thursday so that a meeting may take place.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks that visitors come on Thursday so that a meeting may take place; a homely detail of welcome.

selected.text: From the glad tidings of deputizing in pilgrimage, utmost joy was attained.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá expresses joy at the glad tidings of deputizing in pilgrimage.

selected.text: With the assured leaf, his wife, you have permission to visit the Holy Shrine
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer to visit the Holy Shrine with his wife, the assured leaf.

selected.text: It is my hope that some day you may come to the Holy Spot and meeting be realized
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes that some day the correspondent may come to the Holy Spot and meeting be realized; a simple expression of anticipated reunion.

selected.text: though it be contrary to wisdom, leave hath been granted for a visit of three days
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants a three-day visit though it be contrary to wisdom.

selected.text: Although the condition of this land is not known, yet permission hath been granted.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants permission although the condition of the land is not known.

selected.text: Permission for circumambulation of the Ka'bah of the Divine Purpose is granted to you.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants permission to circumambulate the Ka’bah of the Divine Purpose.

selected.text: God willing, in a seasonable time, permission will be given to thee to come to the East.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises permission to come to the East in a seasonable time.

selected.text: Be sure to show attention and consideration to the divine friends who come for pilgrimage.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that attention and consideration be shown to friends who come for pilgrimage; care for visitors.

selected.text: God willing, you will attain to pilgrimage and witness kindness and be freed from formality.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes the believer will attain pilgrimage, witness kindness and be freed from formality; a distinctive note on the spirit of the visit.

selected.text: You dwelt for a time in the Holy Land and were present at God's feast in the meadow of Akka
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalls that the believer dwelt in the Holy Land and was present at God’s feast in Akka.

selected.text: You have permission to visit the Holy Shrine, may my spirit be sacrificed for its threshold.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants permission to visit the Holy Shrine, adding “may my spirit be sacrificed for its threshold”.

selected.text: Now they must be occupied with service and defer pilgrimage to the Holy Shrine to another time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directs that certain believers occupy themselves with service and defer pilgrimage; service placed before the journey.

selected.text: God willing, whenever I return to the Holy Land, thou shalt have permission to attain My presence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises permission whenever He returns to the Holy Land; places permission within His own travels.

selected.text: However, at present there is an important matter at hand - you must come quickly to the Holy Land.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá summons a believer to come quickly to the Holy Land because of an important matter.

selected.text: If you feel that separation may destroy you, you are permitted to come for a visit for some days.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a visit of some days to one who feels separation may destroy them; shows permission given out of compassion.

selected.text: You, along with some of the friends, have permission to attain Our presence at the end of winter.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer and some friends to come at the end of winter.

selected.text: You hastened with soul and body and found no rest until you reached the vicinity of the Holy Shrine.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes one who hastened with soul and body until reaching the Shrine.

selected.text: In this prohibition [from visiting Haifa] there is a providence which will become manifest before long.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assures that in the prohibition from visiting Haifa there is a providence soon to become manifest.

selected.text: O servant of God! Give thanks to God, for thou hast come to the Holy Land, visited the Sacred Threshold
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids a believer give thanks for having come to the Holy Land and visited the Threshold.

selected.text: Jinab-i-Yusuf Khan arrived and today set out for America. May he be confirmed and assisted, God willing.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports Yusuf Khan arrived and has set out for America, praying he be confirmed.

selected.text: Although you did not arrive, may you be counted among those who attained and among the accepted pilgrims
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays that one who did not arrive be counted among those who attained and among the accepted pilgrims.

selected.text: you entered the Spot of Paradise and attained the presence and saw and heard the call of the Wronged One
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a believer they entered the Spot of Paradise and saw and heard the call of the Wronged One.

selected.text: Those two believers who asked permission to visit the Holy Shrine are permitted to do so with their son.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits two believers to visit the Holy Shrine with their son.

selected.text: After you are released from military service, you have permission to attain the presence of the Holy Land.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a visit after the believer is released from military service.

selected.text: And after you have established your affairs and renewed the means of livelihood, you have permission to come.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a visit after the believer has established their affairs and renewed their livelihood.

selected.text: You asked permission to hasten to these regions during Naw-Ruz with Jenab-i-Khajeh Ibrahim. You have permission.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer to come at Naw-Ruz with Khajeh Ibrahim.

selected.text: as for Jasim, he is permitted to come on condition that he remain in Akka for three days, as I am away in Tiberias
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits Jasim to come for three days in Akka while He is away in Tiberias.

selected.text: Thou hast written regarding thy coming to the Holy Land; do not hasten, for then thou mayest travel with comfort
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá counsels one coming to the Holy Land not to hasten so the journey may be comfortable.

selected.text: it was presented before the Master and the sun of permission shone forth for them to proceed to the Most Great Prison
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh reports that the sun of permission shone for certain believers to proceed to the Most Great Prison.

selected.text: For now, postpone it until such time as Shah Khalil resolves to visit the Promised Land - you too are then permitted.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks a believer to wait until Shah Khalil resolves to visit, and then to come too; permission tied to a companion.

selected.text: Despite the prohibition on entry, out of consideration and kindness toward you permission for his presence was granted
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants presence despite the prohibition on entry out of kindness to the correspondent.

selected.text: It is not permissible for anyone to journey to this land at present. We shall inform thee when it becomes permissible.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that no one may journey to the land at present and promises notice when it becomes permissible.

selected.text: Regarding thy presence, at this time, in this Brilliant Spot--it is not in accord with the wisdom revealed in the Book.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that presence at this time is not in accord with the wisdom revealed in the Book.

selected.text: At the appropriate time, God willing, we will grant you permission for pilgrimage. [At present] wisdom requires this.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises permission for pilgrimage at the appropriate time, saying wisdom requires waiting at present.

selected.text: Permission for presence dependeth upon the exigencies of wisdom. If circumstances warrant, they may present themselves
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh states that permission for presence depends on the exigencies of wisdom; a concise principle.

selected.text: Jinab-i-Aqa Mirza Abbas Khan and the handmaid of God Sakinih have permission to attain the presence in the coming spring
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits Mirza Abbas Khan and the handmaid Sakinih to come in the coming spring.

selected.text: Some of the friends intended to visit the Holy Land, but hindrances prevented them and they have deferred their coming.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports that friends who intended to visit were prevented by hindrances and deferred their coming.

selected.text: As for the matter of severing ties from that land and being present at the luminous Spot, it is not fitting at this time
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says severing ties with one’s land to come and live at the luminous Spot is not fitting at this time.

selected.text: I will certainly grant permission to you and your gracious son to circumambulate the Holy Shrine, but be somewhat patient
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises certain permission for a believer and his son to circumambulate the Shrine but asks for some patience.

selected.text: As to thy coming to this land, there is no harm in that. Thou art permitted to come and this is an ample reward unto thee.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a visit and calls that permission itself an ample reward.

selected.text: Now he has been given permission and leave to return and to be gladdened by the sight of the beloved faces of the friends.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants leave to return and be gladdened by the faces of the friends.

selected.text: Then did the Sun of permission shine forth from the horizon of the heaven of thy Lord's command, the Almighty, the Powerful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describes the Sun of permission shining from the horizon of the Lord’s command.

selected.text: you attained the blessing of pilgrimage to the sacred dust and made the soil of His threshold the healing balm for your eyes
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes one who made the soil of the threshold a healing balm for their eyes.

selected.text: Blessed art thou for having attained the presence of God time and again, and for having inquired of Him in this remote prison.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blesses one who attained His presence time and again in the remote prison.

selected.text: Your beloved daughter and the apple of your eye has been honored to visit the Holy Land and has made the pilgrimage on your behalf
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a parent that their beloved daughter visited the Holy Land and made the pilgrimage on their behalf.

selected.text: And regarding some friends who were not outwardly granted permission for attaining the presence - this was due to divine wisdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh explains that some friends were not outwardly granted presence because of divine wisdom.

selected.text: God willing, in the coming year His Honor 'Ali-Rida Khan will be enabled to visit the Holy Threshold and meet with 'Abdu'l-Baha.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes that ‘Ali-Rida Khan will visit the Holy Threshold and meet Him in the coming year.

selected.text: If possible, proceed with the utmost joy and delight to the path of the Friend - you have permission for attaining the presence
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids the believer proceed in joy and delight on the path of the Friend, with permission to attain presence.

selected.text: His honor Aqa Husayn-'Ali, nephew of Safi-'Ali Shah, has permission to attain the presence whenever travel arrangements are ready
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a named nephew of Safi-‘Ali Shah to come whenever travel arrangements are ready.

selected.text:
After I return, the means may be in place for thee to attain thy highest desire and with Zíbandih
Khanum visit the Holy Threshold
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá hopes that after His return the means may allow the believer and Zibandih Khanum to visit the Holy Threshold.

selected.text: Two days ago your son came and was specifically requested, and for some time was present and honored before the Beloved's presence
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh reports a son who came and was honoured for some time before the Beloved.

selected.text: You had asked permission to come into my presence. I too am extremely eager, but your presence there is very necessary at present.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says He too is extremely eager to meet, but the believer’s presence where they are is very necessary.

selected.text: if any one of them is able to travel with perfect ease and joy and delight, they have permission to visit the blessed resting place
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits any of a group who can travel with perfect ease, joy and delight to visit the blessed resting place.

selected.text: Now he has been granted leave from the precincts of the seat and resting place of the Most Great Throne to return to those regions.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá records leave granted to a believer to return from the precincts of the Most Great Throne to his regions.

selected.text: However, do not hasten pilgrimage to the Holy Land, for his presence in those regions during these days is necessary and obligatory
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá counsels not to hasten pilgrimage, because the believer’s presence in those regions is necessary and obligatory.

selected.text: In these days, permission is not given to anyone, but purely for your sake, permission is given to the two sons of Aga Mirza Khalil.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says permission is given to no one these days, yet purely for the correspondent’s sake grants it to two sons.

selected.text: At the appointed time, which accords with consummate wisdom, permission for attaining the presence shall also be granted, God willing.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises permission at the appointed time that accords with consummate wisdom.

selected.text: My longing to see thee is even more ardent than thine. God willing, in due course permission will be granted - rest assured thereof
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declares His longing to see the correspondent more ardent than theirs and promises permission in due course; sets the theme of shared longing.

selected.text: Although in these days travelling to the land of the heart's desire is not permitted, thou and Mrs. Maxwell have permission to come
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer and Mrs. Maxwell to come although travel to the Holy Land is not generally permitted.

selected.text: If there is some delay in granting permission for some to attend at this blessed spot, this is due to the wisdom set forth in the Book
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that delay in granting permission is due to the wisdom set forth in the Book.

selected.text: I know the ardor which enflames you both with the desire to present yourselves in the Sacred Place and I desire, also, to see you both.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá acknowledges the ardour of two believers to come and says He also desires to see them; mutual longing in plain words.

selected.text: Praise be to God that thou didst arrive in the Most Great Prison and didst attain the presence of the Wronged One in thy comings and goings
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh praises God that the believer arrived in the Most Great Prison and attained presence in comings and goings.

selected.text: the Most Merciful, when He was established upon the throne of His Great Name. Blessed art thou, O servant, for having emigrated in the path of God and for having drunk the choice wine of revelation from this Great Sea
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blesses a servant who emigrated in God’s path and drank the choice wine of revelation.

selected.text: After the return of my brother, if the means for comfortable travel are ready and available, you have permission to come into my presence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a visit after His brother’s return if comfortable travel is ready.

selected.text: Once again thou hast come to visit this exile, and donned the pilgrim's garb to circumambulate the gathering-place of the Concourse on High
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá greets one who has come once again in the pilgrim’s garb to visit the exile.

selected.text: Whenever your hearts become constricted there, you are welcome to come visit the Holy Shrine at any time you wish - you will be most welcome
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá welcomes visitors to the Holy Shrine whenever their hearts become constricted; pilgrimage as consolation.

selected.text: As the route is disturbed and ease of travel is not possible, therefore be patient and postpone your intention of pilgrimage to another time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks for patience and postponement because the route is disturbed and travel cannot be easy.

selected.text: You have the thought of traveling to Iran. This is very blessed. My hope is that after visiting the Holy Land you will be successful in this.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá blesses a plan to travel to Iran and hopes it will succeed after a visit to the Holy Land.

selected.text: You had sought permission to come into the presence, but wisdom does not permit it at this time as these regions are very hot in these days
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declines a visit at present because the regions are very hot; heat named as a reason of wisdom.

selected.text: I long to see them all, but the time is not favorable. Whenever an opportunity arises and there is no difficulty, permission will be granted.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá longs to see them all though the time is not favourable, and promises permission when an opportunity comes.

selected.text: You had sought permission to attain His presence. For now, show patience and forbearance. In the future, God willing, permission will be granted.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks one who sought permission to show patience and forbearance, promising permission in the future.

selected.text: Regarding your spring travel, if you make a journey to Germany and come from there to the Holy Land, that would be suitable. You have permission.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá approves a spring journey to Germany and then on to the Holy Land.

selected.text: We have given thee permission and have recorded for thee the reward of attaining His presence through My Most Exalted Pen in My perspicuous Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants permission and records for the believer the reward of attaining His presence in His Book.

selected.text: As for your request for permission regarding the mother of Inayatu'llah, He said that this year, due to certain considerations, it is not advisable
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says that for certain considerations a visit by the mother of Inayatu’llah is not advisable this year.

selected.text: We have granted thee permission and have revealed for thee that which will draw thee to the Most Exalted Horizon, this glorious and wondrous station.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants permission and reveals words to draw the believer to the Most Exalted Horizon.

selected.text: As for their request for pilgrimage, it was accepted by proxy for that beloved one. We beseech God to accept the deeds, and surely they are accepted.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh accepts a pilgrimage by proxy for a beloved one and prays the deeds be accepted.

selected.text: if there is no obstacle or hindrance, and it is easily possible, put on the garment of presence and attain the honor of visiting the Sacred Threshold
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids one with no hindrance to put on the garment of presence and visit the Sacred Threshold.

selected.text: Regarding the beloved's journey, permission has been granted that they may proceed whenever they wish. This is glad tidings from this servant to you.
selected.reason: The writer sends glad tidings that a beloved one may proceed whenever they wish.

selected.text: The Persian gentlemen and Faruqi are proceeding toward their destination to perfume their faces and hair with the dust of the holy and fragrant shrine
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports Persian gentlemen and Faruqi setting out to perfume their faces with the Shrine’s dust.

selected.text: After several years, we have given Jinab-i-Mirza Mahram and Jinab-i-Zarqani leave to circumambulate the Centre round which circle the Concourse on High.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá gives Mirza Mahram and Zarqani leave after several years to circumambulate the Centre of the Concourse on High.

selected.text: If undertaking affairs requires going to Istanbul, permission is granted. Otherwise, you have direct permission for pilgrimage to the Most Exalted Shrine
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a journey to Istanbul if affairs require it, otherwise direct pilgrimage to the Shrine.

selected.text: You had expressed your utmost desire to attain the presence of the sacred threshold of the One Who conversed on Sinai. Permission for presence is granted.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants presence to one who desired the Threshold of the One Who conversed on Sinai.

selected.text: Your honored son Aqa Muhammad-Rida has repeatedly attained the presence of God on your behalf, and now as your representative circles round the Holy Shrine.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports a son who has repeatedly attained presence on his parent’s behalf and now circles the Shrine for them.

selected.text: Your letter was received. The honored mother attained the privilege of visiting the Holy Threshold, and you too are permitted to attain His presence whenever possible in the future
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports a mother’s visit to the Holy Threshold and permits the child to come whenever possible.

selected.text: And you yourself had requested permission to attain the presence. At present, the wisdom of the Cause of God requires that you not leave those regions empty
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says the wisdom of the Cause requires that the believer not leave those regions empty.

selected.text: Don your pilgrim garb for the Ka'bah of the intended goal and turn your face to the circumambulation point of the Supreme Concourse, for you have permission.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids the believer don the pilgrim garb and turn to the circumambulation point of the Supreme Concourse, for permission is given.

selected.text: Say: None is permitted to turn toward the prison quarter. Thus hath the Tongue of Revelation decreed and the Pen of God, the Beloved of the worlds, recorded.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh decrees that none is permitted to turn toward the prison quarter; a firm statement of prohibition.

selected.text: It would be very good if before going to Iran you could pass by the Holy Shrine - perhaps through God's help and grace one hour of meeting would be possible.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá suggests passing by the Holy Shrine before going to Iran, hoping for an hour of meeting.

selected.text: Permission is granted for you to visit the Threshold that is the sanctuary of the Supreme Concourse. Blessed art thou and glad tidings be unto thee for this.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants permission to visit the Threshold and adds “Blessed art thou”.

selected.text: Permission was previously granted for the journey of Aqa Muhammad Isma'il and thyself, however it must be carried out according to the requirements of wisdom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalls an earlier permission for a journey but says it must be carried out according to wisdom.

selected.text: We have therefore granted thee permission to proceed to this exalted quarter. In any case, shouldst thou desire to journey to this quarter, thou art permitted.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants permission to proceed to the exalted quarter whenever the believer desires.

selected.text: We had given permission to you both aforetime to turn towards the countenance of God, the Mighty, the Praised, but the time passed until the occasion was gone.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh notes that permission given to two believers lapsed because the time passed until the occasion was gone.

selected.text: Therefore, with the blessing of these words of yours, you are permitted to don the pilgrim's garb of the Ka'bih of the divine purpose and make one journey here.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits, through the blessing of the correspondent’s words, one journey to the Ka’bih of the divine purpose.

selected.text: Although at this time, due to wisdom, permission for visits is not being granted, yet the Persian friends are permitted to come, but two by two or three by three.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits the Persian friends to come two by two or three by three though visits are not generally granted.

selected.text: Jinab-i-Aqa Siyyid Asadu'llah has requested permission for you to travel to the western lands to spread the divine fragrances and arise to exalt the Word of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports a request that a believer travel to the western lands to spread the divine fragrances and exalt the Word of God.

selected.text: As for thy father and mother, they are highly respected by Abdul-Baha but their presence in the Holy Land is not presently in accordance with wisdom. Let them wait.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá honours the correspondent’s parents yet says their presence is not now in accordance with wisdom; respect and refusal together.

selected.text: Haji Iman traversed mountain and desert, crossed wilderness and sea, until he arrived at the blessed, luminous Shrine and prostrated himself at its most holy threshold
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes Haji Iman crossing mountain, desert and sea to prostrate at the Shrine’s threshold.

selected.text: Husayn hath appeared before Our presence and circumambulated the House, attaining unto that which was inscribed in the Books of God, the Lord of the seen and the unseen.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh records that Husayn appeared before Him and circumambulated the House as inscribed in the Books.

selected.text: Praise God that you laid your head at the Sacred Threshold and fell prostrate upon the dust of the Court, turned toward the Divine Presence and sang songs of thanksgiving
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praises one who laid their head at the Threshold and sang songs of thanksgiving.

selected.text: Regarding your request for permission to attain His presence, be patient for now. God willing, it will be granted at the appropriate time. At present, wisdom requires this
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks patience over a request for presence, promising it at the appropriate time because wisdom requires waiting now.

selected.text: As for the arrangements for the visit, with wisdom it depends upon drawing lots and the consent of both parties, for if all were to set out at once it would cause disputes.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says arrangements for a visit depend on wisdom, drawing lots and mutual consent, for if all set out at once disputes would follow.

selected.text: Whenever the ways will be opened and the means will be fully provided by which thou mayest travel in perfect comfort and ease then thou hast permission to present thyself.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits presence whenever the ways open and the means allow travel in perfect comfort and ease.

selected.text: He has requested permission for presence during this journey. You should write a letter to him wherever he may be on my behalf stating that he has permission for presence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks the correspondent to write on His behalf to a traveller wherever he may be that he has permission.

selected.text: His honor Aqa Mirza 'Abdu'l-Husayn, with utmost eagerness, enthusiasm and speed set out to visit the Blessed Shrine. However, before reaching its vicinity he was prevented
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports one who set out eagerly for the Shrine but was prevented before reaching it.

selected.text: Those souls who have requested permission to circumambulate the gathering-place of the Supreme Concourse are permitted, provided they are able to come and return in comfort.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits those who asked to circumambulate the gathering-place provided they can come and return in comfort; the return as part of the condition.

selected.text: At this hour the luminary of permission hath dawned from the Dayspring of divine Will, and We have commanded that Jinab-i-Husayn, thy helper, appear by proxy before the Face
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh commands that a helper appear by proxy before the Face.

selected.text: Whenever it is suitable I will give thee permission and consent to come to these parts, but now thou must stay in America and become the cause of the guidance (of the people.)
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a believer to stay in America and become a cause of guidance before permission is given.

selected.text: God willing, I shall later grant you permission to attain My presence, and you shall enter the blessed shrine and attain to the circumambulating-point of the Concourse on High.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises later permission to enter the blessed shrine and reach the circumambulating-point of the Concourse on High.

selected.text: We have commanded Mishkin, upon him be the Glory of God, Lord of the worlds, to present himself before the Countenance through you and to visit Him Who hath spoken and speaketh
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh commands Mishkin to present himself before the Countenance and visit Him Who hath spoken.

selected.text: You had sought permission to come. In truth, you are worthy to don the pilgrim's garb for the sanctuary of the Desired One. However, wisdom must still be observed
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells one who sought permission that they are worthy to don the pilgrim’s garb yet wisdom must be observed; opens the guide’s tension between worthiness and wisdom.

selected.text: You had requested permission by telegraph for a visit … therefore it would be better if you postpone this journey to autumn so that you would be here at the beginning of winter
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá advises one who telegraphed for permission to postpone the journey to autumn so as to arrive at the beginning of winter.

selected.text: Jinab-i-Yusuf is permitted to come into the presence, and if your continued presence there is not absolutely necessary and obligatory at present, you are also permitted to come.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits Yusuf to come and the correspondent too if their presence at home is not absolutely necessary.

selected.text: He endured the hardships of paths by land and sea to attain the presence before the Face of the Wronged One. Praise be to God, he arrived and was blessed with meeting and hearing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh reports a believer who endured hardships by land and sea and was blessed with meeting and hearing.

selected.text: And concerning what thou didst write regarding pilgrimage to the House of God and seeking permission - it is clear that benevolent deeds have ever been beloved in the sight of God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh answers a request about pilgrimage to the House by recalling that benevolent deeds have ever been beloved of God; links pilgrimage to service.

selected.text: As for the travelers, they have not been and are not commanded to stay in that land, for if people gather there from outside it will become the cause and reason for certain events.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh explains that travellers are not commanded to stay in that land, as gatherings from outside would cause events; shows concern for the community’s safety.

selected.text: But if he were to travel for a while, it would be better than staying put. Surely peace of mind will result. And whichever direction he desires and prefers to travel would be proper.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá advises that travel for a while would be better than staying put and would bring peace of mind; travel as remedy.

selected.text: Thou hast asked for permission to present thyself with thy dear husband in this Blessed Spot. In these days it in not according to wisdom. Postpone this matter until some other time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks a wife wishing to come with her husband to postpone because it is not now according to wisdom.

selected.text: O you who thirst for the pure waters of pilgrimage to the sacred threshold, hasten to the spring that is the circling-place of the Supreme Concourse. You are permitted and accepted.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls one who thirsts for the waters of pilgrimage to hasten to the spring, permitted and accepted; a memorable image of welcome.

selected.text: Thou hadst requested permission to visit the holy tomb; at present there are some obstacles. For now, occupy thyself with diffusing the divine fragrances until the appointed time comes
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá postpones a visit because of obstacles and asks the believer meanwhile to diffuse the divine fragrances; waiting filled with service.

selected.text: All the holy leaves are visiting the Sacred Threshold of the Divine Unity on your behalf and as your representatives. Rest assured this visitation is accepted, beloved and praiseworthy.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assures that all the holy leaves are visiting the Threshold on the believer’s behalf and that this visitation is accepted.

selected.text: At this moment the permission to return hath dawned. Turn thy face toward thy native land. Rejoice thou in this irrevocable decree, the Mighty, the Wise. Return by God's might and power
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh announces that permission to return has dawned and bids the believer go home by God’s might.

selected.text: As to thy desire to attain the presence of the Countenance, We have granted thee permission for what thou didst wish, as a bounty from Us unto thee, that thou mayest be of the thankful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants a desire to attain the Countenance as a bounty, that the believer be of the thankful.

selected.text: Regarding the handmaiden of God, Farrukh, thou hadst written that she desires to attain His presence that she may engage in service. For thy sake, permission for her presence is granted.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants Farrukh’s wish to come and serve for the sake of the correspondent who asked.

selected.text: Thou hadst requested permission to attain the Holy Threshold. In these days, the tests and trials in the Desired Land are severe, therefore I have postponed thy presence to another time
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá postpones a visit because tests and trials in the Desired Land are severe.

selected.text: In any case, send her here now for pilgrimage to the Holy Shrine and for a change of climate, and after being honored by pilgrimage and obtaining rest and health, she can proceed to Iran.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that a woman be sent now for pilgrimage and a change of climate, then proceed to Iran once rest and health are restored.

selected.text: the Supreme Threshold! Jinab-i-Ardeshir, like a lion, made his way to the luminous forest and, like a fierce lion, reached these thickets. In this wilderness he roared, and at the Supreme Threshold he offered worship
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likens Ardeshir to a lion who reached the Threshold and offered worship there; a vivid image of arrival.

selected.text: You had requested permission to turn towards the Land of Purpose [Holy Land]. At present wisdom does not permit it. Be patient. I hope the time will come and this desire will be fulfilled.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says wisdom does not now permit the journey and hopes the desire will be fulfilled in time.

selected.text: If there is no obstacle and the means of travel are prepared, thou art permitted to make a trip to the Holy Land, if thou wishest. All the members of the family are very eager to meet you.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a trip if no obstacle exists and adds that the whole family is eager to meet the traveller; warmth within a practical condition.

selected.text: Thou didst seek permission to attain His presence. At this time it hath been granted, and the luminary of permission hath dawned and appeared from the horizon of the heaven of God's command.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh announces that the luminary of permission has dawned from the horizon of God’s command.

selected.text: thou and thy respected wife are permitted to come next summer, but for others the time is not yet appropriate; wisdom does not allow it. Their presence will be more suitable at another time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a couple to come next summer while others must wait, since wisdom does not yet allow their presence.

selected.text: Therefore, permission is granted for you to attain the presence of the Most Glorious Threshold and the circling-place of the Supreme Concourse, may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants permission to attain the Most Glorious Threshold, the circling-place of the Supreme Concourse; a full statement of welcome.

selected.text: And if he insists on traveling to this direction, temporary permission is granted for him to make pilgrimage to the Holy Threshold and spend a few days in fellowship with me before returning.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants temporary permission to one who insists on travelling, for a few days of fellowship before returning.

selected.text: The Most Exalted Pen beareth witness to thy acceptance and thy turning towards Him and thy arrival and thy standing before the gate that was opened unto all who are in the heavens and on earth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s Pen bears witness to the believer’s arrival and standing before the gate opened to all.

selected.text: Several days ago, permission to return was granted to the travelers and emigrants. We beseech God that He may enable all to reach their homes and destinations with the utmost joy and fragrance
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh records permission for travellers to return and prays they reach home in joy and fragrance.

selected.text: The letter of Bashir brought the glad tidings of your intention to make pilgrimage … At that time, if thou canst obtain permission from the postal administration, then undertake the pilgrimage
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá welcomes news of an intended pilgrimage and permits it if leave can be obtained from the postal administration; employment entering the decision.

selected.text: although the yearning for attainment unto His presence blazes in the heart, yet now is not the time for his presence, as there are obstacles and impediments. Let it be postponed to another time
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá acknowledges that yearning blazes in the heart yet obstacles mean it is not the time, and postpones the visit.

selected.text: O pilgrim to the Sacred Threshold … Blessed are they that have attained the Sacred Threshold! Blessed are they that have made pilgrimage to the Spot circled round by the Concourse on High
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá blesses those who attained the Sacred Threshold and made pilgrimage to the Spot circled by the Concourse on High.

selected.text: Regarding visiting at this time, since the summer air in these parts changes due to severe humidity and various illnesses overcome strangers, postpone the pilgrimage to the cool days of winter.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá postpones a visit to the cool days of winter because the humid summer brings illnesses upon strangers; care for the traveller’s health.

selected.text: Now that thou art returning, thou must journey back with the utmost joy and gladness, and praise the Pure Lord, and open thy tongue in thanksgiving that thou hast been favored with such a bounty.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids a returning pilgrim travel back in joy, praise God and give thanks for the bounty; the duty of the return.

selected.text: Thou didst seek permission to proceed to the Holy Shrine in company with Hakim Harun. Permission had already been granted for him. If he hath not yet departed, thou art permitted to accompany him.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer to accompany Hakim Harun if he has not yet departed.

selected.text: Concerning your presence in the Holy Land: these days it is impossible. Whenever the way is open and the means are available; in order to travel with ease and comfort, you have permission to come.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says presence is impossible these days but permits it whenever the way opens and the means allow comfortable travel.

selected.text: Meeting with the friends and visiting the beloved ones is 'Abdu'l-Baha's greatest joy, but these days do not permit it. When the appointed time has passed, permission for pilgrimage will be sent.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls meeting the friends His greatest joy, though the days do not permit it, and promises permission after the appointed time.

selected.text: Permission is granted. However, since there will be crowds during the Ridvan Festival, it may perhaps cause you some hardship. If you can bear the hardship, very well; otherwise, come after Ridvan.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants permission but warns of Ridvan crowds and suggests coming after the Festival if the hardship cannot be borne.

selected.text: Verily, thy coming, at this time, unto this shining, blessed Holy Land is not consistent with wisdom, but when the (proper) time cometh, we shall give thee permission to come to this Spot of Light.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says coming now is not consistent with wisdom but promises permission to come to the Spot of Light when the time comes.

selected.text: Regarding thy desire to attain the presence and meeting, approach from the direction of the Great City is not permitted, but if approached from another direction there is and hath been no objection.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh forbids approach from the Great City yet allows another route; shows how a specific route affects permission.

selected.text: In it was written that you have permission to attain the presence, and this permission was specifically granted to you. Many requested this bounty but due to wisdom it was not granted in these days.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that the believer’s permission was specifically granted while many others were refused for wisdom.

selected.text: As to the mention made of Darvish Husayn who desired to come and sought permission - in these days these regions are somewhat disturbed, therefore we beseech God to grant him the reward of pilgrimage.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh, as the regions are disturbed, prays that Darvish Husayn be granted the reward of pilgrimage instead of the journey.

selected.text: Thy presence here would be contrary to caution in these days … Be assured that, as soon as circumstances permit, thou shalt be summoned here without a moment's delay, for I am most eager to meet thee
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls a visit now contrary to caution but promises an immediate summons when circumstances permit, for He is eager to meet.

selected.text: We testify that Jinab-i-Ism-i-Jud previously visited the House of God on your behalf, and this year they also intend to do so. God willing, they shall attain and be adorned with the seal of acceptance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh testifies that a believer visited the House of God on the correspondent’s behalf and will again.

selected.text: God willing, whenever circumstances arise that permit your absence from there, you will be immediately informed so that you may don the pilgrim's garb to the Friend's lane and attain the greatest honor
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises to inform the believer immediately when circumstances permit their absence, so they may don the pilgrim’s garb.

selected.text: You are longing to meet and are impatient and restless, but what can be done when in these regions wisdom prevents your presence and we are bound by that. Therefore, defer your coming to another time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá acknowledges the believer’s impatience and restlessness but says wisdom prevents presence and He is bound by it.

selected.text: Since harm in coming and going has befallen the very root of the Tree of the Cause, We have therefore forbidden the friends from attaining the presence - otherwise We would have commanded all to attend
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh states that harm from comings and goings has reached the root of the Tree of the Cause, so the friends are forbidden, otherwise all would be summoned.

selected.text: You had requested permission for the presence of Jinab-i-Ghulam-Rida and Jinab-i-Aqa Husayn and their noble children. Now is not a suitable time. God willing, permission will be given in the coming year.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá postpones the visit of two named believers and their children to the coming year.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits three brothers to come during the pilgrimage season when they visit the Ka’bah.

selected.text: Thou didst request permission to attain Our presence. In these days divine wisdom doth not permit such permission to be granted. Be patient, for thy Lord is the All-Patient, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says divine wisdom does not permit permission now and bids patience, for the Lord is All-Patient, All-Knowing, All-Wise.

selected.text: Forbid the loved ones of God from turning toward this direction. Say: O friends, harm befalleth the root of the Tree through your coming and going. Beware lest ye transgress the bounds set forth in the Tablets
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells the friends that harm befalls the root of the Tree through their coming and going and warns them not to transgress the bounds of the Tablets.

selected.text: Aqa Siyyid Nasir has arrived in the Holy Land and attained the honor of circumambulating the Sacred Tomb. We are sending him to you so that by beholding his countenance you may find joy, delight and gladness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sends Siyyid Nasir back after his visit so that beholding him the friends may find joy; return as encouragement.

selected.text: And regarding Aqa 'Ali who is in the great city and has sought permission to attain the presence - permission was granted. Inform him and give him the glad tidings that he may turn towards the Most Holy Court.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants Aqa ‘Ali of the great city permission and asks that he be given the glad tidings.

selected.text: permission was granted from the Source of Authority for your honor to turn toward the intended destination. Now once again this most exalted and most holy command hath descended from the heaven of divine will.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh renews an earlier permission to proceed to the intended destination as a command from the heaven of divine will.

selected.text: O wise Siyavash! You had intended to circumambulate the Holy Threshold and had donned the pilgrim garment of the Friend's sanctuary. This intention will, God willing, be accepted at the Court of the Divine Unity
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells Siyavash, who intended to come in the pilgrim garment, that the intention will be accepted.

selected.text: You had asked permission to attain the presence. For now engage in teaching. After achieving success and victories, God willing, the means will be provided and you will be honored to attain the Sacred Threshold
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids a believer engage in teaching first, after whose victories the means will be provided to attain the Threshold.

selected.text: Therefore, permission is granted that in winter, with the utmost longing and eagerness and complete yearning, you may attain the honor of visiting the blessed Spot, the Sacred Threshold, on behalf of 'Abdu'l-Baha.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a winter visit to the Sacred Threshold on His own behalf, with longing and yearning.

selected.text: I await your coming and that of your respected daughters either this spring or next spring. You will certainly come, and when coming, if possible pass through Stuttgart, Germany and from there come to the Holy Land
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá awaits a mother and her daughters this spring or next and suggests passing through Stuttgart on the way.

selected.text: Jinab-i-Aqa Siyyid Ali, the nephew of His Holiness the one ascended unto God from Manshad, has permission to come, on condition that he comes and attains the honor of visiting the Holy Threshold, returns to Shiraz
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a nephew of a martyr from Manshad to come on condition that after visiting the Threshold he return to Shiraz.

selected.text: This year, in view of the sorrow that hath occurred, if His honor 'Ali-Shir should delay and make his pilgrimage to the Ultimate Goal and Most Exalted Summit in another year, it would be more fitting and appropriate.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh suggests that in view of a sorrow that occurred, ‘Ali-Shir delay his pilgrimage to another year; grief shaping timing.

selected.text: Although the presence of these persons will, in these times, cause the revolt of the heedless ones and increase the trouble, yet for your sake we will send them a telegram to Egypt and permit them to come and visit.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá agrees for the correspondent’s sake to telegraph permission to certain persons despite the trouble their presence may cause.

selected.text: The honored handmaiden of God, the wife of Aqa Siyyid Aqa the physician, along with the sister of the honored martyr, are permitted to come if arrangements can be made for them to travel in complete comfort and joy.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits two named women to come if arrangements allow travel in complete comfort and joy.

selected.text: His honor Aqa Siyyid Nasru'llah, like the messenger of Saba, arrived at the center of the throne of the Most Glorious Beauty (may my spirit be sacrificed for His resting place) and attained the blessing of circumambulating the gathering place of the Supreme Concourse
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likens Siyyid Nasru’llah’s arrival to that of the messenger of Saba.

selected.text: Concerning what was written about Aqa Muhammad Mihdi, upon him be God's peace, permission is hereby granted according to His command that he may proceed to the prison and thence to whatsoever God willeth and desireth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh permits Aqa Muhammad Mihdi to proceed to the prison and thence wherever God wills.

selected.text: The honored Mr. Remey and Mr. Latimer, accompanied by Aqa Mirza Habib and Mirza 'Azizu'llah Khan, have arrived in the Holy Land and, after several days' stay in the utmost joy and delight, have now returned to America.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reports that Mr. Remey and Mr. Latimer visited in joy for several days and returned to America.

selected.text: We bear witness that he hath turned towards Us and traversed land and sea until he reached the Most Great Prison, the Spot wherein the Wronged One was established upon the throne of utterance with manifest sovereignty.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bears witness that a believer traversed land and sea to reach the Most Great Prison.

selected.text: Despite obstacles and difficulties, you have borne every kind of hardship from distant places to attain the blessing of pilgrimage to the Holy Shrine of the Exalted One and circumambulation of the Sacred Resting Place.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praises pilgrims who bore every hardship from distant places to visit the Shrine of the Exalted One.

selected.text: It is never permissible for anyone to come without permission, although many souls have turned towards the Most Holy Court this year without permission. We beseech God to assist them in what He loves and is pleased with.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declares it never permissible to come without permission, though many came that year, and prays they be assisted.

selected.text: Although the time is not propitious and there are impediments to being in His presence, nevertheless, since thou hast beseeched and insisted with the utmost humility and self-effacement, there is no choice but to accept.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá yields to one who begged with utmost humility and self-effacement despite impediments.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits one believer now and another after his return, so both are not present at once.

selected.text: You had hoped for a visit - this intention and resolve is most praiseworthy. However, if there were no obstacles, the Holy Land is in turmoil these days. God willing, you will be granted permission at the appointed time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praises the intention to visit as most praiseworthy while explaining the Holy Land is in turmoil.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says it weighs heavily on Him to withhold permission, citing the saying that necessities permit exceptions; His own burden in refusing.

selected.text: As to their mention of the honored Aqa Siyyid Muhammad-i-Sahhaf, he hath been granted permission to enter. Let him give thanks unto God for this manifest bounty. However, taking up residence in this land is another matter.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh grants Aqa Siyyid Muhammad-i-Sahhaf permission to enter but distinguishes visiting from taking up residence.

selected.text: The Sacred House desired to turn towards God, the Lord of all worlds. We withheld the Pen from giving permission, but at this hour the sun of Will hath shone forth from the horizon of loving-kindness and We have permitted her
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh records that permission once withheld was granted at this hour as the sun of Will shone from the horizon of loving-kindness.

selected.text: And now, O beloved of My heart! Thy letter arrived repeatedly, news arrived, and praise be to God, the morn of hope hath dawned, in that, praise be to God, the Sun of loving-kindness hath risen and permission hath been granted.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a beloved correspondent that after repeated letters the morn of hope has dawned and permission is granted.

selected.text: For a long time thou didst have the longing to visit the Blessed Spot and the yearning to meet this imprisoned one. Finally this gift became realized, but it was for one moment and as the dew to the rose-garden of the hearts
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes a long-awaited visit fulfilled for one moment, as dew to the rose-garden of hearts; a memorable image of brief arrival.

selected.text: you turned towards Him and, purely for the sake of God, set out from your home intending to reach the Most Great House of God. You bore the hardship of travel and traversed sea and land until you arrived at the Most Great Prison
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalls a believer who set out for God’s sake and traversed sea and land to reach the Most Great Prison.

selected.text: Although I have the utmost longing to see you and seek this joy with all my soul, the wisdom of the Cause requires that you exercise some patience and stillness. God willing, you will be granted permission at the appointed time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá expresses utmost longing to see the believer yet asks patience and stillness for the wisdom of the Cause.

selected.text: Therefore, you are given permission to present yourself at the Divine Threshold, and for one day, two days, three days - nay, for one month - seek refuge at this Threshold and find rest in the vicinity of the mercy of the Lord.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants permission to seek refuge at the Threshold for a day, two, three, even a month, and find rest near the Lord’s mercy.

selected.text: This is a book from the Wronged One of the horizons to one of His friends who emigrated from his place until he attained the most exalted horizon and drank the Kawthar of reunion from the hands of the bounty of the Lord of Names.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh addresses a friend who emigrated and drank the Kawthar of reunion from the hands of bounty.

selected.text: Regarding thy visit to this region, it is not permissible at this time. But when the time comes, permission will be granted thee to present thyself at this Source of Light and Dawning-Point of the love of thy Lord, the Forgiver.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises that when the time comes the believer may present themselves at the Dawning-Point of the love of their Lord.

selected.text: God willing, that honored one shall strive with the utmost endeavor in these matters, and if at any time circumstances should require it - that is, if it would in no way conflict with wisdom - he may turn toward the Most Holy Court.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says the believer may come only if it in no way conflicts with wisdom, after striving in the matters entrusted to him.

selected.text: to your intention to visit the House - this is acceptable and beloved in the sight of this Wronged One, provided it be undertaken in a spirit of joy and radiance and be not contrary to wisdom
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh accepts an intention to visit the House provided it is undertaken in joy and radiance and not contrary to wisdom; states the twin conditions of joy and wisdom.

selected.text: The honored Haji, your father, arrived in the Most Great Prison and attained the supreme bounty and infinite mercy by achieving the blessing of attaining His presence and was honored by visiting the purified tomb and illumined shrine
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a son that his father reached the Most Great Prison and visited the illumined shrine.

selected.text: O pilgrim to the circling-place of divine ones! Praise be to God that you traversed long distances and crossed mountains, deserts and seas until you reached the shelter of the Intended One and kissed the threshold of the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Concerning thy presence in the Land of Desire, for the present postpone (this matter) for some later time until the arrival of summer and the passing of frosty winter. At that time it will be acted upon according to the circumstances.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá postpones a visit until summer, after the frosty winter; season and circumstance in one decision.

selected.text: Regarding what you wrote about coming to the Holy Threshold - in these days your presence is needed in those regions, and in the Holy Land turmoil is successive from all directions. Therefore we will summon you at the appropriate time.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that the believer’s presence is needed in their own regions while turmoil surrounds the Holy Land.

selected.text: Regarding pilgrimage to the Holy Shrine - if it can be accomplished with complete security, comfort, and joy during the pilgrimage season, it would be most acceptable. But if it would cause hardship and attacks from enemies, be patient.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá finds pilgrimage acceptable if made in security, comfort and joy during the season, but counsels patience if it would bring hardship and attacks from enemies.

selected.text: Thy letter was received. The contents indicated that thou hast the utmost love towards Mr. and Mrs. James Kehler and dost ask permission to come together and be honored with a visit to the Holy Threshold. For thy sake I give permission.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer to come with Mr. and Mrs. Kehler for the sake of their love.

selected.text: Thou hadst asked permission to attain the presence. If it is possible with the utmost joy and fragrance, and if comfort of heart and soul is ready in presence and return, thou art permitted. Otherwise, wait until the means are provided.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a visit only if joy, fragrance and comfort of heart are ready for coming and return, otherwise to wait for the means; a clear statement of readiness.

selected.text: Now since affairs in this land are in turmoil, therefore the journey of that honored one is difficult. God willing, through divine grace and favor, permission will hereafter be granted at the appropriate time according to what is desired.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh says the journey is difficult while affairs are in turmoil and promises permission hereafter at the appropriate time.

selected.text: And since whatever hath befallen thee was in the path of God, therefore there is no harm if thou desirest to turn toward the Most Holy Court - it is beloved. In all conditions thou hast had and hast permission either to remain or to return.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells one who suffered in the path of God that turning to the Court is beloved and that they may remain or return.

selected.text: As to what you wrote requesting permission to bring someone with you, this was presented and permission was granted. You may bring whomever you wish. Verily our Lord, the All-Merciful, heareth and answereth, and He is the Near, the Watchful.

Also, shouldst thou desire to go to Jibal from there, that, too, is permissible. Or shouldst thou wish, we could obtain a place specially for thee in Haifa
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá leaves the choice of travel to Alexandria, Cairo, Port Said, Beirut or Haifa to whatever improves the believer’s health; care for health as counsel.

selected.text: Know thou with certainty that the longing of 'Abdu'l-Baha is greater than thine. I continually beseech from the threshold of the Ancient and Ever-Living Lord with fervent supplication that He may ordain, in a time near at hand, the beholding of that radiant countenance, and that wisdom may accord with permission for attaining the presence. … But for now, show some patience, for we have forbidden all from attaining Our presence
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá affirms that His longing exceeds the believer’s, prays that wisdom may accord with permission, and asks for patience because all are forbidden for now.

selected.text: and didst seek permission to attain his presence, meeting, and circumambulation as his deputy. This matter was illumined with the light of permission even before being mentioned. When thou seest him, stand before him and proclaim "Allah-u-Akbar" on My behalf and say: Blessed art thou, O thou who art exiled in the lands for the sake of God, the Lord of creation! In these days there hath been revealed from the heaven of utterance of the Lord of religions that which causeth joy and gladness to the people of the cities of justice and fairness. Whenever thou desirest, act as deputy and representative. Thus hath the decree of permission been sent down from the heaven of God's command, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh permits a believer to act as deputy for another and to proclaim “Allah-u-Akbar” on His behalf; a full account of representation.

selected.text: Write to My Afnan [who had promised to escort the Bab's wife] that we agreed and consented to the exalted leaf's request. Currently, the honored persons continue to stand ready and prepared to fulfil that promise, though they have not spoken of it." He further stated, "Write of this matter to the Afnan, upon him be the glory of God, as he was well aware of such a promise beforehand. We desired to fulfil what We had assured the exalted leaf
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh consents to the exalted leaf’s request and wishes to fulfil what He had assured her, with the Afnan to escort her.

selected.text: According to the promise thou didst make to thy respected wife, thou art hoping to visit the threshold of the All-Forgiving Lord. However, complete thy work in such a way that there will be no need for supervision. Then, according to thy promise, put on the pilgrim's garb of the peerless sanctuary and set out for the threshold of the Desired One with the utmost joy, gladness, attraction, exultation, and abundant humility and submissiveness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells one who promised his wife a pilgrimage to complete his work so it needs no supervision, then set out in joy, humility and submissiveness.

selected.text: Regarding moving from San Francisco to New York, it is very suitable. Spend some time there in the utmost joy and fragrance with the friends, occupy yourself with the remembrance of God, and attend to organizing your affairs so that after the war, if it becomes possible to travel in complete comfort and no disruption occurs in Mr. Ralston's affairs, but rather everything remains in perfect order after departure, you have permission to come. Otherwise, no.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá approves a move to New York and permits a visit after the war only if travel is comfortable and Mr. Ralston’s affairs remain in perfect order.

selected.text: Regarding his turning towards this direction, they stated that although this land appears outwardly tranquil, it is inwardly turbulent. The people of this region have been and continue to be utterly perfidious. In the holy Books of the past, the inhabitants of these lands were likened unto the offspring of vipers. This hath been and remaineth the reason for withholding permission; otherwise, this Wronged One hath ever loved not to deprive His loved ones of His presence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh explains that the land, outwardly tranquil, is inwardly turbulent and its people perfidious, the reason for withholding permission, though He loves not to deprive His loved ones.

selected.text: For some time, his honor Mirza Muharram, who is named Manzar, upon him be the most luminous glory of God, was circling in this Most Great Prison around the garden of the Ancient Beauty, and the gardens of his heart and soul were verdant and flourishing through the spring rains of grace and the brilliant rays from the Sun of Truth. Now, God willing, with permission granted, he must pass like the life-giving fragrances of the love of the Lord God to other lands and regions
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes Manzar’s heart flourishing in the Prison and sends him onward like life-giving fragrances to other lands; carries the fruit of the visit outward.

selected.text: Regarding what you wrote about his honor Mirza Yusif Khan - last year you had requested permission for him to attain the presence. Since you had offered the utmost praise and commendation of him and had requested permission for him to visit the Holy Shrine, therefore, in consideration of his connection to the brilliant star of the glorious horizon, his honor Vahid-i-Farid (may my spirit be a sacrifice for the near ones), despite the general prohibition, permission for his presence was granted and a letter was written to you at that time regarding this matter.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that despite the general prohibition Mirza Yusif Khan was permitted because of praise for him and his connection to Vahid-i-Farid.

selected.text: Diverse multitudes and countless throngs each year separate themselves from friend and acquaintance, kith and kin, wife and child, abandoning their familiar homeland, traversing deserts and crossing vast distances until they reach the earthly Ka'bih - an edifice metaphorically attributed to God which, through a word from the Dayspring of Revelation, has become the point of circumambulation for souls. With utmost eagerness, humility and submissiveness they circle round it, seeking acceptance at the threshold of the Almighty and hoping to attract the gaze of the Ever-Living, the All-Powerful.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes multitudes leaving kin and homeland to circle the earthly Ka’bih in humility; places the outward journey within a wider frame.

selected.text: And the other daughter, the leaf of faithfulness who is in Mashhad, has permission to attain the presence. … As to the handmaiden of God, Ziya'ul-Hajiyyih, who is gladdened by the glad-tidings of God: she, along with other handmaidens, has permission to attain the presence next year and come to the blessed and luminous Shrine in the spring. Likewise, Jinab-i-Mirza Salim Khan, Jinab-i-Muhammad Mahdi Mirza, Jinab-i-Haji Majid Arab, and Jinab-i-Masihi - convey to them with utmost longing the Most Wondrous and Most Glorious greetings from Abdul-Baha. They too have permission to attain the presence next year
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants presence to a daughter, to a handmaiden with others next spring, and to named believers next year, with longing greetings; a family-wide permission.

selected.text: Jinab-i-Mashhadi Isma'il, upon him be the Glory of God, arrived. Praise be to God, he was enkindled with the fire of love and spoke in remembrance of the Peerless Friend. The grace of God, exalted be His glory, took hold of him, for his pilgrimage and turning was accepted, even though he set out on the path without permission. However, henceforth you must observe the command, meaning prevent souls from disobedience. None should come without permission. The prohibition has been clearly revealed in the divine Tablets. If anyone comes without permission, their harm will be many times greater than their reward.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh accepts the pilgrimage of Mashhadi Isma’il who came without permission yet forbids it henceforth, warning that harm then exceeds reward; a narrative with its qualification.

selected.text: regarding what you wrote about Haji Muhammad-Baqir and Aqa Siyyid Muhammad-'Ali, upon them be the Glory of God - that they arrived in Beirut and afterwards, without permission from the Dayspring of Grace, proceeded to the prison land - He said: Although it occurred without permission, yet He is verily the Kind, the Compassionate. We beseech God to adorn all with the ornament of permission and then to honor them with His presence, for the fruits of this are countless and will continue to be. And likewise He said: O servant of God! Those souls who are turned toward and gazing upon the Truth and moved by His will must obtain permission from their location. This is true permission
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh pardons two who came without permission and teaches that true permission is that obtained from one’s own location; a distinctive explanation of permission.

selected.text: As to permission for the aforementioned one and two others, there hath never been any doubt that this Revelation hath loved and continues to love the presence of the friends, and seeketh for them the bounty of nearness and meeting, and the feast of revelation and witnessing. However, in this land, following the clamor raised by the previous governor, some discussion hath arisen, as hath been revealed in the Tablets from the Supreme Pen. We have therefore withheld permission for the friends, except for those souls who had previously been blessed with the effulgences of the lights of the Luminary of permission. Now, should wisdom require it, they may proceed; otherwise, God shall record for them the reward of attaining His presence in His decisive and perspicuous Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh explains that this Revelation has always loved the presence of the friends but permission was withheld after the governor’s clamour, with the reward of presence recorded for those prevented.

selected.text: And concerning your request for permission to attain His presence, excellent is that which you have asked, for all have been created for this most mighty, most great, most exalted, most excellent Cause. This servant, in accordance with your wish, on one of the nights of the blessed month of Ramadan, made mention of it before the Throne of the All-Merciful, and this answer was revealed from the Dayspring of God's Command: "O servant present! Write to him who hath turned towards God - upon him be My Glory - that these regions are in turmoil. The fire which the deniers have kindled with their own hands and inflamed by their own deeds hath not yet been extinguished. The world is afflicted with the consequences of its actions, and none hath known or knoweth the cause and reason thereof. Under such circumstances, his movement and journey would not accord with the requirements of wisdom
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh praises a request to attain His presence yet answers that the regions are in turmoil from fires the deniers kindled, so the journey would not accord with wisdom.

selected.text: Both in the language of verses and in Persian the wisdom, meaning and details thereof have been revealed. Nevertheless, in most lands that which has occurred has occurred. For example, some time ago a person intended to go to the regions of Iran. This servant was himself present in the Most Holy Court when the Ancient Tongue verbally counseled him that he must conduct himself with the utmost wisdom and not speak except what God has decreed in the Tablets. Nevertheless, in these days several petitions have reached the Most Holy Court mentioning details about him that are the cause and reason for corruption, conflict and contention in the world. … Consider, for instance, that despite the explicit prohibition revealed in numerous Tablets, every day a group arrives and a group departs, and some of these souls upon returning to every city and land speak contrary to what God has commanded them
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recounts a traveller counselled to wisdom whose conduct caused contention, and groups who come against prohibition and speak contrary to God’s command on return.

selected.text: Permission is granted for the presence of Master Muhammad-Rida, Ali-Akbar son of Master Javad, and Ali-Akbar Iskaui.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá grants presence to three named believers, an example of permissions naming individuals.

selected.text: the utmost love and kindness towards you, therefore are you being informed: O thou who thirsteth for the living waters of the sea of bounty, hasten to the shore of the Most Great Ocean! O thou who longest to inhale the holy fragrances, turn thyself toward the blessed sanctuary
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá summons one thirsting for the sea of bounty to hasten to the shore of the Most Great Ocean and turn toward the blessed sanctuary.
